The speaker mentions looking at Google 10 years ago and feeling it was too rich in valuation, leading him to take a pass on the investment.

thesis: This episode offers a retrospective view on two major technology companies, noting that Microsoft provided zero returns for an investor holding from 1999 to 2012 and that Google was previously considered too richly valued to invest in. The discussion is limited to these specific historical valuation observations rather than a broader market strategy.

claims.claim: The speaker states that Microsoft flatlined for 13 years after 2000, lost a huge portion of its value, and provided zero returns if held from 1999 to 2012.
claims.quote: Microsoft then flatlined all the next 13 years. In fact, it didn't flatline. It was a lost a huge portion of its value and then came back. But basically, you held it from 99 to 2012, you basically had like zero returns.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions looking at Google 10 years ago and feeling it was too rich in valuation, leading him to take a pass on the investment.
claims.quote: So if I look at Google or maybe Microsoft 10 years ago and even then felt that it was too rich in valuation, which would have been a mistake, and I took a pass, which is probably exactly what happened.
